question: Your extraction system reads supplier contracts and emits a finding when a payment clause seems to conflict with the purchase order. Developers of the downstream payables system dismiss many of these findings as false positives. After three months, the team exports all dismissed findings to learn which kinds of clauses cause them, but it cannot group the findings in any useful way. Each finding stores only a field name, a severity and a free-text message. What is the most likely cause of this problem?

options.text: The team sampled too few dismissed findings, and a larger stratified sample would reveal the clause types that cause false positives.
options.reason: The guide uses stratified sampling to measure error rates, and a larger sample still lacks the triggering construct, so the dismissals stay ungroupable.

options.text: The findings lack a calculated total extracted alongside the stated total, so the system cannot flag discrepancies in the payment amounts.
options.reason: The guide uses calculated_total next to stated_total to flag discrepancies in one extraction, which does not show which constructs cause dismissed findings.

options.text: The findings do not record which construct in the contract triggered them, so dismissals cannot be grouped by a detected pattern.
options.reason: The guide says a detected_pattern field that records the triggering construct is what enables systematic analysis of false positive patterns when findings are dismissed.

options.text: The validation loop does not append specific validation errors to the prompt on retry, so the model repeats the same mistaken findings.
options.reason: The guide uses retry with error feedback to correct a single extraction, and it does not make dismissed findings analyzable by pattern.
